answer: Slow-Release Identity Bridge: each new identity must maintain a small, continuous outbound task before gaining full participation rights. Reputation accrues like a glacier—slowly, and only after sustained activity across weeks. A single verified credential can unlock one pearl of reputation, but the bridge between new and trusted status stays gated by elapsed real work. Attackers must fund thousands of distinct long-running task slots, paying compute and monitoring costs per identity that never amortize.
